The underlying observable-specific inverse first acquires exact strictly graded generator relations with a factorial envelope. Rational local coefficients and geometric randomization permit exact rational unbiased outputs. Within-grade motion is implemented by a killed signed walk only when absolute diagonal dominance and a microscopic work bound hold; a block inverse is not supplied for free. A two-state transition-simulation example has work times second moment >=1/(144 epsilon); exact local probabilities are a stronger interface. Finite observable closure alone does not remove a slow inverse.

With independent symmetric y or y^-1 multipliers at each copy, the Fourier charge becomes a symmetric walk. Root's internal extension gives sharp Theta(gamma^-1/2) response, O(gamma^-1/2) expected row work and O(gamma^-1) second moment in the stated model. A deterministic (+1,-1) cancelling cycle restores Theta(gamma^-1). These operations change the stochastic dynamics; they do not accelerate inversion of the original unmodified chain.

This permits the (+2,-1) cycle and gives O(1+B/delta+(gamma delta^2)^-1/3) response/work. Explicit graph support, potential verification, coordinate queries and exact arithmetic are charged. Arithmetic is polynomial in bounded charge magnitude, not automatically its logarithm. A row sampler alone cannot verify all support edges.

Classical difference constraints/minimum cycle mean can acquire the potential on an explicitly enumerated graph, at graph-dependent cost. Qualitative positive winding alone is insufficient: a long alternating cycle retains inverse-gamma response through a neutral transient. Physically reciprocal couplings can fail the certificate. Shared Brownian phase, Hill/Airy mechanisms, duality, random Neumann series and matrix recovery are established mathematical baselines; neither broad originality nor a new physical effect is claimed. # Independent construction: inverse of a local observable without global mixing

Date: 2026-10-12. Internal reconstruction and invention attempt. Historical novelty: **UNKNOWN**. No claim below is externally verified. The direction was selected before screening information from other workers.

## 1. Why a generic transition-simulation solution is impossible

Let the state space be {0,1}, let f(x)=x, and take 0<epsilon<=1/4. Kernel P0 has transition probabilities P0(0,1)=epsilon and P0(1,0)=epsilon. Kernel P1 has P1(0,1)=2epsilon and P1(1,0)=epsilon. Both are irreducible reversible two-state chains. Their stationary means are respectively 1/2 and 2/3, a difference Delta=1/6.

The interface is a transition simulator: an algorithm may adaptively choose either state and request a transition from it. It is not given exact transition probabilities. Let T be its number of requests, and Z its output. Couple the algorithm's internal random bits and couple transition replies maximally until the first unequal reply. At state 1 the replies can always agree; at state 0 their mismatch probability is epsilon. If no mismatch occurs before the P0 run stops, both transcripts and outputs agree. Thus the mismatch event D has probability at most epsilon E0[T]. This statement holds for a random stopping time by summing the conditional mismatch probabilities over requests made before stopping.

If the outputs are unbiased under both kernels, then

    Delta = |E[Z1-Z0]| <= E[(|Z1|+|Z0|) 1_D]
          <= sqrt(2(E[Z1^2]+E[Z0^2]) Pr(D)).

Writing M=max(E0[Z^2],E1[Z^2]) and C=max(E0[T],E1[T]), we obtain

    C M >= Delta^2/(4 epsilon) = 1/(144 epsilon).

Consequently no universal bounded-variance, bounded-work, unbiased stationary estimator exists in this interface. The observable is bounded and has Dirichlet energy O(epsilon), so small *positive* Dirichlet energy does not repair the obstruction. A negative-Sobolev/source condition would have to exclude it.

Exact probability queries change the example: query the two rates and compute the stationary ratio. They must not be conflated with simulation access. This bound does not exclude symbolic local-rule algorithms.

# Exact rational evaluator and an honest within-grade extension

Internal proof, 2026-10-12. Historical novelty UNKNOWN. This supplements `PROOF_AND_GATES.md` and uses its notation.

## A. Removing transcendental output from the estimator

Assume all generator coefficients, terminal values, and row-sampling probabilities are rational, with exact rational local access. Fix an integer k>=max(1,A), set rho=k/(k+1), and sample N with

    Pr(N=n)=(1-rho)rho^n, n=0,1,... .

The sampler uses repeated exact Bernoulli(rho) coins. Follow N symbolic successor steps exactly as in the original proof. Return

    Y = W_N t_{I_N} / [(1-rho)rho^N],

or zero if the path terminates first. Every output is rational. With |t|<=T and |W_n|<=A^n/n!,

    E Y = sum_n (K^n t)_i,
    |Y| <= (k+1) T exp(A/rho) <= (k+1) T exp(A+1),
    E Y^2 <= (k+1) T^2 sum_n (A^2/rho)^n/(n!)^2
           <= (k+1) T^2 exp(2A/sqrt(rho))
           <= (k+1) T^2 exp(2A+1),
    E[N+1]=k+1.

The penultimate inequality uses sum_n z^{2n}/(n!)^2 <= exp(2z). The last uses sqrt(1+1/k)<=1+1/(2k) and A<=k. No exponential needs to be evaluated by the implementation; it appears only in the analysis.

Exact rational probability sampling can use uniform random bits to sample an integer in the denominator range, rejecting the top incomplete interval. For an explicitly represented B-bit denominator the expected number of rejection attempts is less than two. The complexity of obtaining that denominator from a row's coefficients is part of row acquisition.

If the bit size and cost of a row at depth n are polynomial in n and the input bit size, then the accumulated rational product has polynomial bit size in n and the input. Geometric N has all moments finite, bounded polynomially in k for any fixed moment. Standard exact arithmetic therefore gives finite expected bit work, polynomial in the declared row parameters and k. A claim of this type is not valid if the row representation itself grows exponentially with depth; that remains a separate gate.

This closes the finite-bit exact-unbiasedness issue for rational data and rational-valued terminal functions. General real-valued functions still require exact-real output or controlled approximation.

## 1. The local scientific model and its acquired observable algebra

Let P be any stochastic matrix on a finite directed network V. The network can have arbitrary feedback and arbitrarily slow mixing; the algorithm has a local row sampler for P and coordinate access to an input vector x with |x_v|<=1. The probabilistic model initially takes |x_v|=1. There is one circular phase y=exp(i theta), where theta evolves by Brownian motion on the circle with generator gamma*d^2/dtheta^2, gamma>0. At rate one, each active phase x_v independently chooses w~P(v,.) and is replaced by

    x_v <- y x_w.

This is a compact-state Feller jump-diffusion. Multiplication is nonlinear in the joint state. The same single phase can be reused on every edge and every feedback cycle. No large moment closure is supplied or acquired.

For phi_vk=x_v y^k, k>=0, direct local generator calculation gives

    L phi_vk = -(1+gamma k^2) phi_vk + sum_w P_vw phi_w,k+1.      (1.1)

Brownian motion contributes -gamma k^2, the active refresh contributes -phi_vk, and the replacement contributes y^(k+1)x_w. Other active-site updates do not affect phi_vk. Positive Fourier charge strictly increases even when the same phase is reused; unlike Boolean parity, y^2 does not erase it.

Put d_k=1+gamma k^2 and

    w_n = product_{k=0}^n d_k^{-1}.

Then the explicit response operator is

    h_v(x,y) = sum_{n>=0} w_n y^n (P^n x)_v.                    (1.2)

Only one walk on P is needed to evaluate a random term. This is an exact symbolic interface acquired from (1.1), independent of the number of possible joint phase configurations.

## 2. Domain, stationary centering, and the time-integral meaning

The series in (1.2) converges uniformly: w_n has at least factorial tails for any fixed gamma>0. Its first two theta derivatives also converge uniformly because multiplication by n or n^2 does not defeat these tails. The active jump part is a bounded operator on continuous functions. Thus h belongs to the generator's domain; alternatively one can use closedness of the Feller generator and the partial-sum identity

    L h^(N)_v = -x_v+w_N y^(N+1)(P^(N+1)x)_v.

The remainder tends uniformly to zero. Therefore

    -L h_v = x_v.                                               (2.1)
